propositions: The Git version floor gate step reads .github/git-version-floor.txt from the patchset tree but exits hard when absent, causing every in-flight change branched before the file landed to fail regardless of content.
Gerrit's Verified lane runs the workflow definition from the target branch but checks out the patchset tree, creating a definition-vs-tree skew where the gate step exists but its data file may not.

The gate should treat an absent floor file as no-floor-declared and skip with an explanatory log line naming the skew cause and rebase remedy, rather than hard-failing and sending authors hunting for a file they never touched.
An under-floor Git version must still fail with a diagnostic naming required version, installed version, and upgrade path, with enforcement unchanged when the floor file is present.
